videos.title: Low-Latency Strix Halo Cluster with RDMA (RoCE/Intel E810) and vLLM, Framework Desktop Boards
videos.description:
In this video, I move beyond Ethernet and llama.cpp and show a 2-node Strix Halo cluster using RDMA and vLLM tensor parallelism. The setup uses two Framework Desktop motherboards with 128 GB of unified memory each, connected directly via Intel E810 cards configured for RoCE.

I cover the hardware details that matter for this build: direct-attached RDMA, custom cooling for the E810, and why running a x16 NIC in a PCIe x4 slot isn’t a real problem for inference. I also compare RDMA latency to standard Ethernet and explain why low latency is the key enabler for tensor parallelism here.

On the software side, I walk through vLLM with Ray and the main blocker I hit along the way: missing RCCL support for gfx1151 in upstream ROCm. I explain what broke, how I patched RCCL to make multi-node tensor parallelism work on Strix Halo, and how to reproduce the setup using my toolboxes.

Timestamps
00:00 – Introduction
01:14 – The Hardware
02:09 – RDMA / RoCE Network Card
03:28 – Custom Cooling for Intel E810
06:22 – PCIe Lane Caveat (x16 to x4)
08:32 – ROCm / RCCL gfx1151 Support
10:31 – Configuration Tutorial
13:06 – Benchmarks
14:03 – Conclusion

Links & Resources
- Strix Halo Toolboxes & Guides: https://strix-halo-toolboxes
- vLLM Strix Halo Toolboxes (patched RCCL): https://github.com/kyuz0/amd-strix-halo-vllm-toolboxes
- vLLM Benchmarks: https://kyuz0.github.io/amd-strix-halo-vllm-toolboxes/
- vLLM Tensor Parallelism: https://developers.redhat.com/articles/2025/02/06/distributed-inference-with-vllm#gpu_parallelism_techniques_in_vllm

videos.title: Running vLLM on Strix Halo (AMD Ryzen AI MAX) + ROCm Performance Updates
videos.description:
This video is divided into two parts: a technical guide on running vLLM on the AMD Ryzen AI MAX (Strix Halo) and an update on the local AI ecosystem four months after launch.

Part 1: vLLM on Strix Halo I demonstrate how to use my new Fedora-based toolboxes to run vLLM on the Framework Desktop and other Strix Halo systems. I compare the Triton and ROCm Attention backends and provide throughput benchmarks for Large Language Models using unified system memory.

Part 2: Strix Halo Ecosystem Update A look at the progress of the Strix Halo platform since August. This includes performance gains in llama.cpp, the current state of image generation with Qwen Image, and video generation with WAN 2.2. I also discuss ongoing ROCm 7 stability work and how to contribute kernel logs to help AMD optimize RDNA 3.5.

Timestamps

In this tutorial, we explain how to install and run locally the vLLM library and how to run Large Language Models (LLMs) using vLLM and Python on Windows. We explain how to correctly install vLLM on Windows by using WSL. We also explain how to run the Qwen model by using vLLM.
